title: Garlic shrimp and mushrooms with ravioli

items: 2 packages (9 oz each) fresh cheese ravioli
1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
8 oz cremini or white mushrooms, sliced ¼ inch thick
1 lb large shrimp, peeled, deveined and patted dry

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt. Season the shrimp with ½ tsp salt and the pepper.
Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer with no fat and cook 6–8 min, stirring only once or twice, until they release their liquid and turn golden brown.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the butter and, once it melts, the shrimp in a single layer. Cook 1–1½ min per side, until pink and opaque. Stir in the garlic for the last 30 sec.
Meanwhile, cook the ravioli as the package says, usually 3–5 min, until they float and are tender. Save ½ cup of the cooking water and lift the ravioli out with a slotted spoon so they don't tear.
Add the ravioli to the skillet with the lemon juice and 2–3 Tbsp of the cooking water. Toss gently until glossy.
Sprinkle with parsley, taste for salt and serve.
tips: The dry pan is on purpose. Mushrooms soak up butter added at the start and steam instead of browning.
Shrimp go from done to rubbery in about 1 min. Pull them as soon as they curl into a loose C shape.
storage: Best fresh. Fridge up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a skillet over medium-low heat with a splash of water just until warm; overheating toughens the shrimp. Don't freeze.
